name: non-mendelian genetics overview
title: Non-Mendelian inheritance: mitochondrial DNA disease passes only through the mother and varies by heteroplasmy and threshold, nuclear mitochondrial disease follows Mendelian patterns, and triple nucleotide repeat disorders (Huntington disease, myotonic dystrophy) are autosomal dominant with anticipation, read by repeat size; each column gives inheritance, presentation, testing and treatment

root.title: Non-Mendelian inheritance: WHAT does the family tree and the patient show?
lines: • high-energy tissues (brain, retina, skeletal muscle, heart) in 2 or more systems → MITOCHONDRIAL
• worse and EARLIER in each generation → triple nucleotide REPEAT (anticipation)

groups.title: MITOCHONDRIAL disorders
lines: ↓ ATP · dual control by nuclear + mitochondrial genes

groups.title: Triple nucleotide REPEAT disorders
lines: autosomal dominant · bigger repeat = earlier, more severe

head: h
Mitochondrial DNA disease
point mutations: MATERNAL · deletions, duplications: sporadic
pres: • HETEROPLASMY: mutant + normal mtDNA, shared out at random
• symptoms once a tissue passes its THRESHOLD

head: h
Nuclear-gene mitochondrial disease
follows MENDELIAN inheritance
pres: • nuclear genes for mtDNA nucleotides or replication
• too little mtDNA → too little energy

head: h
Huntington disease
polyglutamine huntingtin aggregates in neurons
pres: • JUVENILE (60-100 repeats): rigidity, seizures, little chorea
inv: • only after counselling by a geneticist or genetic counsellor

head: h
Myotonic dystrophy
myotonia: cannot relax after contracting
pres: • ptosis · narrow face · balding · cataracts · arrhythmia

rows: • MRI or spectroscopy: lactate peak, basal ganglia, leukodystrophy
• muscle biopsy · mtDNA and nuclear gene panels
• mitochondrial cocktail: riboflavin, coenzyme Q10, thiamine
